summary: Baileys fork pulls author-controlled unpinned dependencies on load and auto-follows author's WhatsApp channel
details: This fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library declares `@xzvbailss/xzgateway: "latest"` as a required dependency and `@xzvbailss/xz-protect: "latest"` as an optional dependency. The `latest` dist-tag is mutable and under the same author's control, with no version pin and no integrity check. `Utils/crypto.js`, `Utils/lt-hash.js`, and `Utils/chat-utils.js` import symbols (`md5`, `hkdf`, `LTHashAntiTampering`, `expandAppStateKeys`) from `@xzvbailss/xzgateway` at top level, so whatever code the author publishes under that name runs inside the installer's process on `require('@xzvbailss/baileys')`. `Socket/index.js` additionally performs `import('@xzvbailss/xz-protect')` when `AnchorGuard` is enabled and passes the live WhatsApp socket to `createAntiBugGuard`. The imported helpers are on the path that derives WhatsApp Noise/AppState encryption keys, so a future publish to either dist-tag can execute arbitrary code with access to the installer's host and intercept the installer's WhatsApp keys. Separately, on every successful connection open the library silently calls `sock.newsletterFollow('120363430764800148@newsletter')` (up to 3 attempts) under the installer's logged-in WhatsApp account, documented only as an opt-out via `autoFollowNewsletters: false`, using the installer's identity for reach-padding of an author-controlled channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
